title: GPRSCDR: Add parser for TimeStamp type
description:
TimeStamp is not decoded as date/time field but as octet string.

This is example to show how TimeStamp is decoded [gtpprime_cdr_sgw_record.pcap](/uploads/336b2eeadd42621d3b484079f60e5198/gtpprime_cdr_sgw_record.pcap)

This is the same timestamp format as GSM SCTS, right? As !18163 notes, this should perhaps be implemented as a common type for times eventually.

Idea is the same but encoding is different:
1. Digits presedense in byte is different.  
For example year 2024:  
TS 32.298 -> 0x24  
TS 23.040 -> 0x42  

2. Encoding of time zone absolutely different  
For example UTC+1hour:  
TS 32.298 -> 0x2b0100 (0x2b='+', 0x01=1 hour, 0x00=00 minute)  
TS 23.040 (page 67) -> 0x40 ( 0b0100=4*15minute=1hour 0b'0'000='+')  

> TS 23.040: The Time Zone indicates the difference, expressed in quarters of an hour, between the local time and GMT. In the first of the two semi-octets, the first bit (bit 3 of the seventh octet of the TP-Service-Centre-Time-Stamp field) represents the algebraic sign of this difference (0: positive, 1: negative).
Or did I incorrectly understand question?

OK, that makes sense.

The cutoff for 90 for determining what century the year is in is your doing? Probably reasonable. 

You probably could get the year through seconds string with `tvb_bcd_dig_to_str_be(actx->pinfo->pool, tvb, 0, 6, NULL, false)` (and also for the hour and minutes), which might be less overall code, though you'd have to still do a check for the year to determine the century.
I have removed centure of year checking. Very unlikely find messages with time before 2000 year.
